- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after a high, then stabilizes), model often fails to recognize this; add a 3–5 day lagged mean-reversion buffer in forecast.  
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., > +0.3) after a downtrend, model often underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to match sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price volatility in early days of the forecast window; apply a 2–3% upward bias to first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
